title: The Fall of the Tubbas and the Miracle of Najran
overview: This episode explores the internal collapse of the Himyarite Kingdom in Yemen, focusing on the tragic assassination of King Hassan by his brother Amr and the psychological toll of that betrayal. It then transitions to the history of religion in the Arabian Peninsula, detailing how Unitarian Christianity reached Najran through the miracles and missionary work of a pious man named Faymiyun.
lessons: Arrogance and blind ambition often lead to illogical decision-making and eventual ruin, as seen in the case of King Hassan.
The acquisition of power through betrayal and sin rarely leads to peace; the 'happy person' is defined by a clear conscience, not wealth or status.
A person should value and protect truthful advisors (like Dhu Ru'ayn) even if their advice is difficult to hear at the time.
Sincere devotion and miracles can be powerful tools for dawah, as shown by Faymiyun’s influence on the people of Najran.
Historical context is crucial for a deep understanding of the Qur'an and the Prophet's ﷺ life, as it explains the origins of the communities he encountered.

chapters.title: The Arrogance of King Hassan
chapters.summary: Following the death of Tibban As'ad, his son Hassan ascended to the throne of Yemen. His reign was initially powerful, but he soon became blinded by arrogance and ambition, seeking to conquer both the Arabs and non-Arabs to become the king of the earth. His advisors were deeply concerned when he declared his intention to invade the Persian Empire and kill its ruler, the Kisra. They realized his plans were unrealistic and dangerous for the safety of Yemen, yet Hassan's pride prevented him from listening to reason.
key_points: Hassan ibn Tibban As'ad succeeded his father as the Tubba of Yemen.
Hassan planned to conquer the whole earth, starting with the Persian Empire.
The Persian Empire was considered the most powerful nation at that time.
Ministers viewed Hassan’s ambition as mad and detached from reality.

chapters.title: The Assassination Plot
chapters.summary: The ministers of Yemen, fearing that Hassan's plans would lead to the destruction of their kingdom, decided to assassinate him. They approached his younger brother, Amr, who was the only person Hassan trusted enough to allow into his chambers without being searched for weapons. To persuade Amr, they promised him the kingship of Yemen. Despite a grave warning from a minister named Dhu Ru'ayn about the psychological consequences of fratricide, Amr's greed led him to stab his brother with a concealed dagger.
key_points: Amr ibn Tibban As'ad was the king's younger brother and only trusted confidant.
The ministers used the promise of power to incite Amr to commit murder.
Dhu Ru'ayn was the only advisor who opposed the assassination plot.
Hassan was killed in his private chambers by Amr.

chapters.title: Amr's Guilt and the Wisdom of Dhu Ru'ayn
chapters.summary: After becoming king, Amr fell into a state of severe clinical depression and chronic insomnia caused by the guilt of killing his brother. Unable to find a medical cure, he was told by advisors to execute the conspirators who had egged him on. When it was Dhu Ru'ayn's turn to be executed, he presented a sealed letter containing poetry he had given to Amr before the murder. The poetry reminded Amr that Dhu Ru'ayn had actually advised against the crime, leading the king to spare his life while the others were executed.
key_points: Amr suffered from debilitating insomnia and depression after the assassination.
Dhu Ru'ayn had given Amr a sealed letter (amanah) before the crime.
The poetry in the letter highlighted that the 'happy person' is the one who can sleep comfortably.
Amr acknowledged Dhu Ru'ayn's truthfulness with the word 'Sadaqta' and pardoned him.

chapters.title: Civil War and the Rise of Dhu Nuwas
chapters.summary: The death of Amr led to a period of political instability and civil war in Yemen as the descendants of Rabiah ibn Nasr fought for the throne. During this chaos, a usurper named Lakhni'ah seized power. However, Dhu Nuwas, a descendant of the Tubba family (Tibban As'ad), eventually managed to enter the palace and assassinate Lakhni'ah. This act restored the rule of the original Tubba dynasty to Yemen, which continued until the introduction of new religious influences.
key_points: A civil war broke out among the royal family for control of the kingdom.
Lakhni'ah was a usurper who briefly disrupted the Tubba line of succession.
Dhu Nuwas was the member of the Tubba family who killed Lakhni'ah.
The restoration of the dynasty marked the end of the immediate civil strife.

chapters.title: The Arrival of Christianity in Najran
chapters.summary: Christianity entered the Arabian Peninsula, specifically Najran, through a man named Faymiyun. He was a Unitarian Christian (Muwahhid) from Sham who was captured by a gang in Africa and sold into slavery in Najran. His owner witnessed miracles while Faymiyun was in prayer, specifically a divine light surrounding him. Faymiyun challenged the local people, who worshipped a sacred tree, to witness whether his God could destroy their idol. After he made a sincere du'a, lightning struck and destroyed the tree, causing the entire city to accept Christianity.
key_points: Faymiyun was a pious Unitarian Christian from Sham (greater Syria).
He was sold into slavery to a man in Najran after being captured in Africa.
The people of Najran originally practiced tree-worship (paganism).
A bolt of lightning destroyed the tree following Faymiyun's prayer (du'a).

chapters.title: The Religious Landscape of Pre-Islamic Arabia
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by summarizing the three main religious influences that were present in Arabia before the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: idol worship, Judaism, and Christianity. Understanding these backgrounds is essential for contextualizing the Prophet's ﷺ later interactions with different groups such as the Quraysh polytheists, the Jews of Madinah and Khaybar, and the Christians of Najran. The speaker emphasizes that these historical origins are frequently referenced in the Qur'an and tafsir.
key_points: Three main groups: idol worshippers, Jews, and Christians.
The Prophet ﷺ interacted with the Christians of Najran during his time in Madinah.
The story of the Najran delegation is mentioned in the tafsir of Surah Ali 'Imran.
Historical background is vital for understanding the Seerah and the Qur'anic narrative.

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn, wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.
Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wanfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: Last week, we spoke about how Judaism entered the Arabian Peninsula,
and we talked about the [[Tubba|تبع]] or the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], who was known as [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]].
And we talked about how he became a Jew when he was passing through [[Madinah|مدينة]] and he met some of the scholars of the Jews there,
and they taught him about Judaism. They taught him about the [[Tawrah|توراة]],
and [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] became a Jew in [[Madinah|مدينة]]. And then he took these two scholars with him back to [[Yemen|اليمن]], and the people of [[Yemen|اليمن]] also accepted Judaism.
Now starting where we left off, when [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] died, when the [[Tubba|تبع]] of [[Yemen|اليمن]], [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], when he passed away,
the kingdom was passed on to his son, [[Hassan|حسان]]. So [[Hassan|حسان]] ibn [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] became the new ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And during the time of [[Hassan|حسان]], during the rule of [[Hassan|حسان]], the kingdom expanded greatly.
And [[Hassan|حسان]] became so powerful to the extent that it made him arrogant. He thought that nobody could touch him.
He thought that he was so powerful that he could do whatever he wants, so this arrogance came into his heart. Such to the extent that he said:

segments.translit: La-aghzuwanna al-ʿaraba wal-ʿajama wa aḥkuma al-arḍ.

segments.text: He said, "I will fight the Arabs, and I will fight the non-Arabs, and I will conquer all of their lands until I rule the whole earth. My goal is to become the king of the earth. I will fight the Arabs, the non-Arabs, I'll do everything, and I will become the king and the ruler of this earth."
So his cabinet ministers and his advisors, they were surprised at this. You know, this is a type of blind ambition that he had, that really was not realistic at all.

And his cabinet members, and his advisors, and his staff, they knew that this was not realistic. They knew that he had just become so blinded by his power and so overcome by his arrogance that he wasn't even making logical sense anymore.
So [[Hassan|حسان]] asked his staff and his cabinet and his ministers, he asked them, "Who is the most powerful nation on the earth right now?"
Who is the most powerful nation on the earth right now? And they replied him by saying they are the Persians. The Persian Empire right now, they are the most powerful nation on earth.

Then he said, "I'll start with them. We will start with them. We will fight them. We will take over their kingdom, and then we will continue on with our conquest of different lands around the earth. So we'll start with the Persians."
"And the first ruler that I will kill will be the [[Kisra|كسرى]] of Persia, the ruler of Persia."
So his cabinet ministers are listening to this speech, and they're saying, "This guy has really lost the plot. This guy has gone mad."
"How can he think that he can go and fight the Persians?" Now, the Persian Empire at that time, it was the most powerful nation on earth.

And these [[Yemeni|يمني]] ministers and advisors, they knew that they weren't powerful enough, that their army was not anywhere close to as powerful enough to be to to fight with the Persians, that they were not at that level. And they knew that that was an impossible task.

So they tried to reason with [[Hassan|حسان]]. They tried to say, "This is ridiculous. There's no way that you'll be able to pull this off. Just forget about this, you know? We don't need to do this. Why do you need to do this?"
But he was so overcome by his arrogance, he was so impressed with himself that he wouldn't listen to anything that anyone had to say.
So they decided that they needed to put a stop to this. The ministers, they knew that he was going down a very dangerous path and that this path would be the destruction of [[Yemen|اليمن]].

So they knew that they had to stop him somehow. So when reasoning failed, when trying to speak to him in a logical fashion, when this failed, they thought of other means that they could use to stop him from carrying out this crazy plan of his.
Now, one thing about [[Hassan|حسان]] is that he was also very, very paranoid. He was paranoid to the extent that he trusted no one.

Even his closest advisors and his cabinet and his staff, none of them could enter his room except after being checked for weapons. He would not let anyone enter his room, even no matter how high of a position they had in his cabinet. Nobody could enter his room unless they were checked for weapons.
And if they were clear, they were allowed to come in and speak to him. This is the level of paranoia that had come to him, and this is how deeply he distrusted everyone.
But there was only one exception to this. There was only one person he trusted fully. And this person could come and see him anytime without being checked or anything. And that was his brother,
his younger brother, [[Amr|عمرو]] ibn [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]].

So [[Hassan|حسان]] was the king, and his younger brother was [[Amr|عمرو]]. So [[Amr|عمرو]] could come in and talk to his brother and discuss things with him, and the security protocol did not apply to him.
So the ministers who wanted to stop [[Hassan|حسان]] from carrying out this plan of going and invading the Persian Empire, they saw this as an opportunity.
First they tried to reason with [[Hassan|حسان]], and when that failed, they went to the [[majlis|مجلس]] or they went to the gathering of his brother, [[Amr|عمرو]]. And they spoke to him.
They said, "Look, we have tried to speak to your brother about calling this crazy plan of his off, but he's not listening to us."

"So we see that the only solution to stop him, the only way that we can stop him from destroying the kingdom of [[Yemen|اليمن]], is that we have to kill him. He cannot continue to be our king with this type of crazy ideas in his head."

And then they said to [[Amr|عمرو]], they said, "Look, you are the only one who can get to him without being checked. You are the only one who can actually physically get close enough to him with a weapon so that you can kill him. None of us can do that because none of us can even enter his quarters without being searched. So this falls on you."

And they said to him, to sweeten the deal, they said, "Look, if you do it, we promise, we all agree, we unanimously agree that you will be the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. We are going to appoint you. You're going to be the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]]."
So the greed and the lust for power entered the heart of [[Amr|عمرو]]. He wanted to be the king. He wanted to have this power and this rule.
So he agreed with them, and they planned to assassinate [[Hassan|حسان]] ibn [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]].

Now, there was only one minister from those ministers who disagreed with this plot, who didn't want to have anything to do with it. All of them agreed except one, and his name was [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]].

And [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] said to [[Amr|عمرو]], he said, "Don't do this. Don't do what they're telling you to do. Do not kill your brother. Nobody can kill their brother except that after that, he will be afflicted with such a guilt and sorrow and depression after that."

"If you go ahead with this, you know, you're just greedy right now, you're just looking at the kingdom, but you will fall into such a sorrow and depression if you kill your brother that none of the kingdom, or none of the wealth, or none of the riches that you have will be of any benefit to you. That depression is just going to eat you alive. Don't do it. Don't do it."
So [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] was the sole member of the cabinet who tried to convince [[Amr|عمرو]] not to go through with this plot to assassinate his brother.
But all of the other cabinet members egged him on and told him to do it, and they beautified this evil action for him by saying that you will become the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]] if you do this.
So in the end, [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] was not able to convince [[Amr|عمرو]] to hold back on the plan. And [[Amr|عمرو]]'s greed and his lust for power got the better of him.

And one day, he went into the chambers of his brother, and of course he went in there without being checked because [[Hassan|حسان]] trusted his brother. And he came in with a dagger concealed under his clothing.
And when he got close enough to him, he actually did stab him, and [[Hassan|حسان]] ibn [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] was assassinated and killed in this manner.

And they kept their promise to him. The ministers kept their promise to [[Amr|عمرو]], and they made him the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. So now [[Amr|عمرو]] is the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. But what happens to him? Exactly what [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] told him would happen to him. He becomes so overcome by sorrow and grief and guilt...
depression overtakes him, and this depression is so bad that [[Amr|عمرو]] is not able to sleep at all in the night. He can't sleep.

And during the day, he is so weak and tired and fatigued because he doesn't have any sleep in the night. So he suffers from such an extreme case of insomnia that he is not able to actually function in his life properly.

Now, before [[Amr|عمرو]] actually went through with the plot to execute his brother, to assassinate his brother, just before the time came for the assassination, [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]], who was trying his best to convince him not to go through with this plot,
he said to him, 'Okay, you're not listening to me, but I'm writing a letter, and I'm sealing this letter and giving it to you as an [[amanah|أمانة]].
So keep this letter with you, and when I tell you to open it, then open it.' So [[Amr|عمرو]] said, 'Okay,' and he kept that letter with him.

And after that, he went ahead with the assassination plot, and he killed his brother. So now, after the assassination, he's suffering from this depression and this sadness, so he calls the best doctors of [[Yemen|اليمن]] and the specialists and everyone to come and try to treat him for this problem that he's having, this lack of sleep.

And all of the doctors and specialists and everyone agreed that the reason why [[Amr|عمرو]] is suffering from this type of depression is obviously because of the evil act that he did, the fact that he murdered his own brother in order to take over his kingdom.

This is something that would destroy anyone psychologically to do such a thing. So all of the doctors and all of the specialists that he brought, they agreed that, 'Yes, the cause of your insomnia, the cause of your inability to sleep, the cause of your depression is because of this crime that you committed, because you killed your brother.'
So [[Amr|عمرو]] said, 'Okay, I understand that. I know what the problem is. That's not what I called you here for. I called you for a solution. What should I do about it now?'

And they said to him, 'The only solution you have is everyone who conspired, everyone who came to you and convinced you to kill your brother, the people who came up with this plan, you have to kill all of them.'

'The ones who made you do this, you have to execute each and every one of them, and then you should be okay.' So he said, 'Okay, no problem. I'll do that. I'll kill every one of them. Everyone who conspired with me to murder my brother, I will kill each last one of them.'

So he started to kill all of those cabinet ministers one by one. He executed them each one by one. And then [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]]'s turn came to be executed. But as we know, [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] was the one who told him not to do it.

But when his turn came, he was about to be executed as well. So [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]], he said, 'Wait, wait. O [[Amr|عمرو]], before you execute me, before you kill me, I just need you to do one thing.' He said, 'Okay, what is that?'

He said, 'Remember, before the assassination, I gave you a sealed letter?' He said, 'Yes, I remember.' He said, 'Okay, I told you to keep that as an [[amanah|أمانة]], to keep that as a trust, and not to open it until I tell you to open it.' He said, 'Yes, I remember that.' He said, 'Okay, now, before you kill me, I need you to open that letter and read that letter.'
So he said, 'Okay.' He took the letter and he opened it, and he found two lines of poetry. Two lines of poetry written on that piece of paper. The two lines of poetry, they said:

segments.ar:
أَلَا مَنْ يَشْتَرِي سَهَرًا بِنَوْمٍ ... سَعِيدٌ مَنْ يَبِيتُ قَرِيرَ عَيْنِ 
 فَأَمَّا حِمْيَرٌ غَدَرَتْ وَخَانَتْ ... فَمَعْذِرَةُ الْإِلَهِ لِذِي رُعَيْنِ
segments.translit: Ala man yashtari saharan bi-nawmin, sa'idun man yabitu qarira 'ayni. Fa-amma Himyaru ghadarat wa-khanat, fa-ma'dhiratu al-ilahi li-Dhi Ru'ayni.

segments.text: So these two beautiful lines of poetry that [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] wrote, it means, 'Who would be crazy enough to purchase the inability to sleep, to purchase insomnia, and buy that with their sleep? Basically, to trade a comfortable night's sleep for the inability to sleep? Who would do that?'

'If you're sleeping comfortably, this is a great blessing. So why would you sell your ability to sleep comfortably and trade it for a life with no comfort? [[Sa'idun man yabitu qarira 'ayni|سعيد من يبيت قرير عين]]—the happy person is the person who is able to sleep comfortably. It doesn't matter how rich you are, it doesn't matter how powerful you are, if you're not able to even sleep in the night, you'll never be happy.'

'Even a person who doesn't have much wealth, he doesn't have much riches, he doesn't have any power, but he's able to sleep comfortably in the night, that's the happy person, rather than the most powerful person in the world who is unable to even sleep in the night. [[Sa'idun man yabitu qarira 'ayni|سعيد من يبيت قرير عين]]—the happy person is the one who is able to sleep comfortably.'

'[[Fa-amma Himyar ghadarat wa-khanat|فأما حمير غدرت وخانت]]—as for [[Himyar|حمير]], [[Himyar|حمير]] means [[Ahl Yemen|أهل اليمن]], the people of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. As for the people of [[Yemen|اليمن]], meaning the ministries, the cabinet, [[fa-ghadarat wa-khanat|فغدرت وخانت]], these people betrayed and committed treason.'

'[[Fa-ma'dhiratul-ilahi li-Dhi Ru'ayni|فمعذرة الإله لذي رعين]]—except [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]]. Except [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]]. [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] is the one who told you not to go through with this. Do you remember that?'

And when he read, when [[Amr|عمرو]] read these two lines of poetry, he remembered the advice of [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] to him before he killed his brother, that he was the only one who told him not to go through with it. But he didn't heed that advice, he didn't listen to [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]], and he went ahead and did it anyways. So once those two lines of poetry reminded [[Amr|عمرو]] of [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]]'s stance on this whole issue, he said, 'Yes, you're right. [[Sadaqta|صدقت]]. You have spoken the truth. And you are pardoned.' And he didn't kill [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]]. So [[Dhu Ru'ayn|ذو رعين]] survived because of that.

So [[Amr|عمرو]] continued as the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]], but when he died, when [[Amr|عمرو]] died, then the fighting started. Then the descendants of [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], who we spoke about last week, they started fighting over the kingdom of [[Yemen|اليمن]].

They didn't think that it should go to the next one in line, rather each one from the royal family thought that they had a claim to that kingdom. So nobody wanted to give it to any other members of the family for rule. So the civil war started. So the family of [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], they started to fight over who should rule [[Yemen|اليمن]] now. And it became so chaotic, it became such a civil war that different factions of [[Yemen|اليمن]] were fighting amongst each other. So [[Yemen|اليمن]] became disunified and it became disunited, and different people were ruling different parts of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and it was just a big mess, it was full of chaos.
So during this period of political instability when there was no central government ruling the country...
some members from the family of the [[Tubba|تبع]] that remained. Of course, they didn't have any political power anymore, but there were still some members of the family that remained.
And one of the members of the family, he was from the descendants of [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], his name was [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]].

And [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] was able to penetrate through the kingdom, or through the palace, with a weapon concealed under his clothes. He was able to come into the kingdom, or come into the palace of [[Lakhni'ah|لخنيعة]] with a weapon.
And he was actually able to stab [[Lakhni'ah|لخنيعة]] with this dagger. So once he killed [[Lakhni'ah|لخنيعة]], then [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]...
...took back the kingdom of [[Yemen|اليَمَن]] again. So the the rule returned to the family of the [[Tubba|تُبَّع]].

So the the rule was with the family of the [[Tubba|تُبَّع]] for so many years and so many generations, and then for a few years it was taken away, and [[Lakhni'ah|لخنيعة]] and his gang took over. But then after some time, [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], who was from the family of the [[Tubba|تُبَّع]], he was able to kill [[Lakhni'ah|لخنيعة]] and get the rule of [[Yemen|اليَمَن]] back to his family.
So the rule of [[Yemen|اليَمَن]] returned to the family of the [[Tubba|تُبَّع]]. And [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] was the new king. [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] was the new king.
All right. Now during the rule of [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], there was an incident that happened in [[Najran|نَجْرَان]].

There was an incident that happened in [[Najran|نَجْرَان]]. And [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] is in present-day Saudi Arabia, it's in the southern part of present-day Saudi Arabia, and it's close to the border of [[Yemen|اليَمَن]]. It's a city close to the border of [[Yemen|اليَمَن]].

And what's important about this city and the people of this city is that during the time of the Prophet ﷺ while he was in [[Madinah|مدينة]], a delegation of Christians came from [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] to meet with the Prophet ﷺ in [[Madinah|مدينة]].

And this story is recounted in the [[tafsir|تَفْسِير]] of Surah [[Ali 'Imran|آل عِمْرَان]]. The delegation of Christians that came from [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] to speak with the Prophet ﷺ in [[Madinah|مدينة]].
So [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] was a city that had Christians. And how did Christianity initially enter into the Arabian Peninsula, and particularly into the city of [[Najran|نَجْرَان]]?

This is important to know, because when we go on with the [[Seerah|سِيرَة]] of the Prophet ﷺ and his time in [[Madinah|مدينة]], and we talk about his meeting with this Christian delegation from [[Najran|نَجْرَان]], we need to know why were there Christians in [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] in the first place.
So the story of how the Christians came into [[Najran|نَجْرَان]], it happened during the time that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] was ruling [[Yemen|اليَمَن]].

There was a man, a Christian, and he was actually a Unitarian Christian. He was a Christian who really believed in the true message of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]]. He didn't worship [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]], and he didn't consider [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]] to be the son of Allah, rather he was a true Christian on the real [[deen|دِين]] of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]].
And they were known as the [[Muwahhidin|مُوَحِّدِين]], meaning the Christians who believed in [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]], they didn't believe in the Trinity.

So there was a man, his name was [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]], and he was a Christian from [[Sham|شَام]], meaning from the greater Syria area, and he was on the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]]. He was on the religion of [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]].

And he used to travel to do [[dawah|دَعْوَة]], he used to go to different places to call people to [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]]. So he was on a trip from [[Sham|شَام]], from greater Syria, he went to Africa. He went to Africa to do [[dawah|دَعْوَة]], to call the people to [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]].
And while he was in Africa, he was captured by a gang. And in those days, you know, there were gangs that used to capture foreigners and then they used to sell them into slavery.

So while [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] was in Africa, he was captured by one of these gangs and he was sold into slavery, and the buyer was a man from [[Najran|نَجْرَان]]. The buyer was a man from [[Najran|نَجْرَان]].

So [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] was captured and he became a slave of this man, and the man, he took him back with him to [[Najran|نَجْرَان]]. So [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] came from greater Syria, he went to Africa to do [[dawah|دَعْوَة]], he was captured, sold into slavery, and now he's headed to [[Najran|نَجْرَان]].

This is the first Christian who entered into the Arabian Peninsula. So now [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] is in [[Najran|نَجْرَان]], and he's a slave. And he accepts that, okay, he's a slave, this was the [[qadar|قَدَر]] of Allah for him, this is what Allah had destined for him.

He was a very pious man, he was a devoted worshipper, and he accepted whatever Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] had written for him. So he was a slave for this man, and he served him as a slave. But whenever he had free time, in the nights and other times that he wasn't working, he would devote himself to [[ibadah|عِبَادَة]].

He would worship Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] whenever he had any free time. And he was such a devoted and pious worshipper of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] actually granted him some miracles.

There are some people from the pious worshippers of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] shows miracles through them, He gives them some miracles, and [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] was one of these people. So one day in the night, he was worshipping Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], he was doing his [[ibadah|عِبَادَة]], and his owner, he comes in the room and he sees that [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] is busy in worship and there is light around him.

And he doesn't know where this light is coming from, there are no candles, or there's no fire or nothing, but there's light all around him while he's worshipping. So when [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] finished his prayer, his owner asked him, "What is this? This is something amazing, something I have never seen before."
So then [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] saw this as an opportunity to give him [[dawah|دَعْوَة]], to give his owner [[dawah|دَعْوَة]].

So he said, "You know, I am a believer in the message of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]], [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]] was the messenger of Allah, this is what he taught us, to worship Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] alone without any associate, without any partner. He told us not to worship any creation, not to worship any idols." He explained to him what [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]] was, and what was the message of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]].

So after explaining this, the owner, he was hesitant, because it wasn't easy for him to admit that the religion that he was following was wrong. So he was hesitant to accept the religion of [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]], his slave, even though he saw with his own eyes this miracle, he saw the light around him while he was doing his [[ibadah|عِبَادَة]].

And during that time, the people of [[Najran|نَجْرَان]], they had a tree that they used to worship and they considered this tree to be their god, the object of their worship. So they used to worship this tree.
So [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]], when he saw the hesitance of his owner from accepting the doctrine of [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]] and the message of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]]...

...he said to him, "Okay, I see that you're hesitant, but let me ask you a question: what do you think if my God destroys your god, meaning that tree, the tree that they used to worship? If my God destroys your god, then will you worship my God?"

And then he said, "In that case, of course. If your God destroys my god, then I will know that, if this tree gets destroyed, then I will know that will be proof that it's not actually a god. So of course, if your God destroys this tree, then definitely I will believe in the message that you are teaching me and I will worship your God."

So [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] said, "Okay, I don't want to do this just in front of you. I want you to gather all of the people of [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] by the tree that you worship, and then I want them all to witness what happens."
He said, "Okay." So he called the people and they all gathered near that tree that they used to worship, and [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] also came.

And he started making [[du'a|دُعَاء]] to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], sincere [[du'a|دُعَاء]] to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], "Ya Allah, guide these people, show them this sign that they are asking for, so that they will know that what they are worshipping is false and is not worthy of worship, and that they will accept You and they will worship You alone." He started making [[du'a|دُعَاء]] and he continued to make it with sincerity and with perseverance.

And then the answer of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] came. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] sent down a bolt of lightning, it hit that tree, and the tree burst into flames. The tree was destroyed, and the whole city of [[Najran|نَجْرَان]] who used to worship that tree, they witnessed this in front of their own eyes.

So when they saw that, they said, "[[Amanna bi-Rabb il-'alamin|آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ]]." They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds, we believe in Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]," and they accepted the religion of [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] and they became Christians.
So this is how Christianity entered the Arabian Peninsula, and in particular...
the city of [[Najran|نجران]]. And the people remained as Christians in [[Najran|نجران]] up to the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
When the Prophet ﷺ was in [[Madinah|مدينة]], the people of [[Najran|نجران]], they were still Christians even at that time.
So this is how Christianity entered the Arabian Peninsula.
So we spoke about in the previous lessons, first we spoke about how idol worship came into the Arabian Peninsula.
Then in the next lesson, we spoke about how Judaism came into the Arabian Peninsula.
And now today we spoke about how Christianity came into the Arabian Peninsula.
And it's very important to know all of these backgrounds because the Prophet ﷺ dealt with all three of these groups of people.
He dealt with the people who worshipped idols, he dealt with the Jews, and he dealt with the Christians.
And you will find the interactions that the Prophet ﷺ had with all of these people, you'll find it in the Qur'an.
You will find instances of how the Prophet ﷺ interacted with the [[mushrikin|مشركين]], the idol worshippers of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
You will find interactions of the Prophet ﷺ with the Jews of [[Madinah|مدينة]] and the Jews of [[Khaybar|خيبر]].
And you will find instances of the interactions that the Prophet ﷺ had with the Christians who came from [[Najran|نجران]].

So it's very important to know all of these to have some background information on this, so that when we get into those interactions [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], when we speak about the Prophet ﷺ and how he dealt with these people, you will have some idea of the origin of these people and how they came about.
And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] next week we will continue speaking about the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ [[bi-idhnillah|بإذن الله]].
